newsitem.title: HAITI: Policeman, resident killed in Haitian capital.
newsitem.headline: Policeman, resident killed in Haitian capital.

text.p: Gunmen killed an off-duty police officer on Tuesday and another man was shot to death in a separate incident this week, raising concerns about security in Haiti's capital.

Officer Mario Joassaint was shot to death on a bus about to leave downtown Port-au-Prince early on Tuesday morning by men who were trying to rob the passengers, Haitian National Police spokesman Felder Jean-Baptiste said.
In the other incident, gang wars in Cite Soleil, a Port-au-Prince slum, claimed a fourth victim in two weeks when a young man was killed on Monday, police said.

Jean-Baptiste said Joassaint, who was not in uniform, was killed and other passengers on the bus were wounded, but could not confirm radio reports that a shootout had taken place between the officer and the robbers.
Two men, one suffering from a gunshot wound, were arrested on Tuesday as suspects in the slaying, he said.

According to human rights reports, eight police officers were killed in a similar style between March and August 1996, usually on public transportation. But police said Tuesday's killing was more likely a case of random crime in which Joassaint intervened.
Residents of Cite Soleil, a giant slum of some 200,000 of Haiti's poorest people, expressed concern about retaliation after Monday's slaying of the young man, whose name was not released.
Some residents have left their homes in the slum to move elsewhere after weeks of constant gunfire and fires set in their aluminium shanties.

"There are gangs from different parts of Cite Soleil," said Christy Jackson, a Cite Soleil resident. "They are fighting over turf to traffic drugs or sometimes they are just settling scores and sometimes they are just drunk."
Gang members can be seen walking through neighbourhoods carrying guns even during daylight hours.
"I close my house up completely once the sun sets," said a grammar school teacher who did not want to be identified.
Police, equipped with inferior weaponry to the automatic weapons sometimes carried by the gangs, have often avoided patrolling the area in the past.
Haitian National Police Chief Pierre Denize said police efforts in the area have been stepped up, and called for more government attention to the social problems of the slum.
